skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: A browser automation skill that documents the agent-browser CLI for navigation, interaction, snapshots, screenshots, and session-based web workflows.
skill.summary: Control web pages through the agent-browser CLI with structured navigation, interaction, and capture commands.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: The skill is a browser automation guide with many expected CLI examples, and several Markdown fence detections were false positives. The real security concern is the documented use of real Chrome profiles, remote debugging, persistent cookies, and authenticated sessions.

remediation.issue: Real Chrome profile and CDP reuse
remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions that point agents at a real browser profile. Use isolated temporary profiles and require explicit user confirmation before CDP access.
Replace the user-specific profile path with a generic placeholder and a warning about private cookies and tokens.
Use neutral example domains and avoid workflows that preserve login cookies for a named service.
Document guardrails for eval, cookies, storage, upload, screenshots, and PDF capture on sensitive pages.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Workflows with Agent Browser
content.value_statement: Agents need reliable browser control without custom scripts. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured commands for navigation, interaction, snapshots, and screenshots.
actual_capabilities: Install or build the agent-browser CLI from npm or source instructions.
Open pages, navigate history, reload pages, and manage browser sessions.
Click, double-click, focus, type, fill, select, check, hover, drag, and upload files.
Extract text, HTML, values, attributes, titles, URLs, counts, boxes, screenshots, and PDFs.
Find elements by role, text, label, placeholder, alt text, title, and test id.
Use waits, scrolling, JavaScript evaluation, cookies, storage, tabs, frames, dialogs, and JSON snapshots.
limitations: Requires Node.js, npm, and the agent-browser CLI to be installed before use.
Element refs are stable only for the current page load and can change after navigation.
Real browser profile and CDP workflows can expose private cookies and logged-in sessions.
The skill does not enforce site permission checks or credential handling safeguards.

use_cases.title: Smoke-test web flows
use_cases.description: Navigate a web app, interact with controls, and verify visible results after each step.

use_cases.title: Give agents page context
use_cases.description: Capture structured snapshots so Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can choose reliable element refs.

use_cases.title: Collect repeatable page evidence
use_cases.description: Extract text, take screenshots, and save PDFs from pages that need recurring review.

prompt_templates.title: Open and inspect a public page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-browser to open the public URL I provide. Take an interactive snapshot and summarize visible navigation, forms, and primary actions.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a simple form safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Open this public form, snapshot the page, fill only the fields I specify, and stop before submitting. Ask before using saved sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a web workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Run through this user flow with agent-browser. Snapshot after each navigation, use stable refs, and report whether each expected page state appears.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an authenticated flow with consent
prompt_templates.prompt: Use an isolated session for this authenticated test. Ask before CDP or real profile access, capture evidence, and avoid reading unrelated cookies or storage.

output_examples.input: Review a public product page and identify the main call to action.
output_examples.output: The page loaded successfully. The primary action is a signup button near the top. Secondary links include pricing, documentation, and support.

output_examples.input: Check whether a dashboard form can be filled without submitting it.
output_examples.output: The form fields were found and filled as requested. Submission was not performed. A screenshot was captured for review.

output_examples.input: Extract visible text and save a page capture for a weekly report.
output_examples.output: Visible headings and summary text were collected. A screenshot and PDF capture were saved for the report workflow.

best_practices: Use isolated sessions for testing and avoid real browser profiles unless the user explicitly approves.
Take a fresh snapshot after every navigation before using element refs.
Restrict eval, cookies, storage, uploads, screenshots, and PDFs to pages the user owns or authorizes.
anti_patterns: Do not point automation at a personal Chrome profile path by default.
Do not run browser commands against logged-in sites without explicit user consent.
Do not reuse element refs after navigation or page reloads.

faq.question: What does this skill help automate?
faq.answer: It helps agents control a browser through the agent-browser CLI for navigation, interaction, extraction, and capture tasks.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require extra software?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires Node.js, npm, and the agent-browser CLI installation steps described by the skill.

faq.question: Can it use an existing logged-in browser profile?
faq.answer: The skill documents that workflow, but it is high risk because it can expose private cookies and sessions.

faq.question: Can it capture screenshots and PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented commands include screenshots, full page capture options, and PDF output.

faq.question: How should element refs be handled?
faq.answer: Create a new snapshot after navigation because refs are stable only for the current page load.
